Version: 1.0 (draft) Date: August 2026 Scope: UI, layout, navigation, theming — declarative application design from text manifests Status: Research and recommendation; not yet a published standard

There is no single existing standard for designing full application UI from a declarative text file. Instead, the problem is addressed in fragments: Docs-site generators (commercial docs platforms, PraisonAIUI, Hugo) declare navigation and layout in config files. Form libraries (JSON Forms, RJSF) declare layout trees from JSON Schema. Agent UI protocols (A2UI, AG-UI) declare streaming component surfaces for LLM-generated UI. Catalog standards (OpenUI, Backstage) declare component metadata without runtime layout. Design token standards (DTCG 2025.10) declare theming without structure. Recommendation: Define an Application Design Protocol (ADP) that synthesises proven patterns from 45 surveyed standards into a UI-only manifest format. PraisonAIUI already implements approximately 60% of this model. ADP formalises, extends, and publishes what exists today.
A protocol that lets a developer (or LLM) describe an application's visual design — pages, navigation, components, themes, routes — in one or more text files, without writing application code.

YAML is the best authoring format for application design manifests.

Commercial docs platforms — the closest docs-site analogues — use JSON config with a published $schema URL for IDE autocomplete. This works well for flat-to-moderately-nested config but becomes verbose for deep layout trees. A2UI uses JSON as both authoring and wire format because LLMs emit structured JSON reliably and ambiguity is unacceptable at runtime. Docusaurus and Gatsby use JavaScript/TypeScript config for programmatic power — but this sacrifices portability and LLM generation safety.

Primary authoring: YAML — best for nested templates / zones trees Alternate authoring: JSON — for teams preferring $schema editor tooling Never at runtime: YAML — always compile to JSON before serve Composition: $yaml: file includes (Backstage), not Helm Go templates Power users: Optional CUE/Jsonnet compiles to YAML before validation Verdict: YAML remains the recommended default, but ADP MUST accept JSON as an equivalent authoring format with identical semantics.

Declarative, not executable — manifests describe intent; runtimes render; no inline code or templating logic in core spec. Schema-first — JSON Schema 2020-12 is canonical; YAML is authoring convenience. Structural strictness — unknown fields rejected in strict mode (K8s CRD pattern). Catalog allowlist — component type must exist in published catalog (A2UI pattern). Envelope consistency — every document uses apiVersion, kind, metadata, spec. Separation of concerns — theme, navigation, components, templates, routes are distinct spec sections. Compile, don't interpret — YAML → validated JSON manifest → static assets at build time. Accessibility by default — catalog entries include ARIA role hints (WAI-ARIA pattern). Versioned protocol — schemaVersion integer + apiVersion string; breaking changes bump version. Extension namespace — x-adp-* prefix reserved; plugins register catalog layers. File composition — $yaml: includes for modular configs (Backstage pattern). Route-driven rendering — URL resolution selects template; no hardcoded layout in renderer.

Existing aiui.yaml (and aiui.template.yaml) files remain valid. Migration steps: Add apiVersion: adp.io/v1alpha1 and kind: Application (optional during transition). Wrap top-level keys under spec: (compiler accepts both shapes during v1alpha1). Rename site fields unchanged; map navigation, templates, routes as-is. Publish catalog; register custom component types via plugin schema layers. See adp/aiui-mapping.md for field-by-field mapping.

Should ADP standardise layout type names (ThreeColumnLayout) or allow runtime-defined layouts? Should navigation support both filesystem-auto and manual tabs in one spec, or require a mode switch? Should agent-driven surfaces (A2UI) be a separate kind: Surface or embedded in Application? Should theme reference DTCG token files directly or use simplified preset shorthand?

ADP is feasible and largely prefigured by PraisonAIUI's existing architecture. The research across 45 standards yields a clear synthesis: Envelope from Backstage/K8s Composition from PraisonAIUI (components → templates → routes) Catalog from A2UI/OpenUI Theming from DTCG Validation from AWP (structural schema + R-rules) Authoring in YAML (default) with JSON alternate (published $schema pattern) Status: Research draft — see adp/implementation-status.md for implementation gaps. The draft spec, JSON Schema files, and example manifests are published alongside this report in docs/protocols/adp/.
